Measures to Improve Fuel Economy. In the NPRM, the NHTSA discussed several methods which could be used by manufacturers of nonpassenger automobiles to improve the average fuel economy of their nonpassenger automobile fleets. These methods included such techniques as technological improvements, weight reduction, and performance reductions. Many comments directed at these discussions of fuel economy improvement techniques were received from manufacturers of nonpassenger automobiles. Virtually all these comments made the point that the NHTSA, in one way or another, had overstated the potential for fuel economy improvement in nonpassenger automobiles.
It is important to put the assessment of fuel economy improvement contained in the NPRM in the proper perspective. The NPRM proposed an average fuel economy standard of 18.7 mpg. This proposed standard was intended to be set at a level that all manufacturers could meet without substantially modifying their product plans for model year 1979. The 18.7 mpg standard also assumed that there would be no adverse fuel economy effects resulting from the emissions standard and fuel economy testing procedures established by the EPA
